x: "Rome was not built in a day", so however enthusiastic the lads are we must wait awhile before they click: and this should be just in time to greet those most promising runners, Alan Black and Ken Miller who soon move up into the Senior ranks.

It was most encouraging to see four of our five runners well placed in the early stages of the race, and even more encouraging to find Alan Black leading the field at half-way, with Ken Miller almost on his heels in sixth place and John Thresher not far away in nineteenth position.
A fast improving Ken Miller won the Junior '5' "Savage Shield". He reversed his Surrey Championship performance(5th to Alan Black's 3rd) by putting Alan a good 300 yds behind him.

After 2½ miles Charlie was 5th, followed by Ken Miller 28th, David Jones 46th, Ranjit Bhatia 53rd, John Moore 60th, Clive Shippen 61st, and Ken Venton 82nd, with the others at regularly spaced intervals within the first half of the field.
Ken Miller brought about a reversal of form when he was first man home in 25th position. He was backed up by Alan Black 67th, Ken Venton 75th and John Thresher 90th.
Ken Miller, dogged by injury during the previous few months had come into the team only during the previous few days, when Malcolm Robinson was forced to withdraw.

We have however the prospect of the return of Jack Brown and the further improvement of many of our runners such as David Jones, Malcolm Robinson, Clive Shippen and Charlie Dabbs, plus juniors Alan Black and Ken Miller who move up to the senior ranks to inspire our hopes for 1960/61.

Ken Miller, Jumbo Masters and Symons of Hercules as a result lost 200 yds or so through going off course. Towl (HHH) was a comfortable winner in 29:53, with Shippen (31:30), Miller (31:35) and Masters (31:40), 3rd, 4th, 5th, Charlie Dabbs (34:40) could not overcome the going and finished an uncharacteristic 15th.
With Ken Miller and Alan Black in the first four after half a mile and Cyril Forey and Mike Heck backing up well, our team chances looked very reasonable.

At 2½ miles, Alan Black was seen to be running very well and easily in 7th place with Ken Miller on his heels in 9th position. Jack Brown was 21st, Charlie Dabbs (without shoes, à la Tulloh) 32nd, Masters 47th, Dooley 57th, Gebbett(recovering from gastric trouble) 60th and Johnston 64th.

Of the eleven Bels that started only Ken Miller produced anything worthwhile, and it was no surprise when we were placed last in the team result; especially so when five of the eleven were in the last eight to finish.

Most improved runners of the season are at present Ken Miller, Alan Black and, Junior Cyril Forey; but perhaps there are some dark horses waiting for the final run-in before they show their hand---Mike Heck, Jim Radford, David Jones and John Thresher for example.

After one mile Ken Miller, Mal and Alan were together around 10th position; and at the end of the first lap these three were still with the leaders, Mal in 2nd place, Alan 10th with Ken just behind; but for fourth scoring man we had to go back to Clive Shippen in 52nd place - seemingly ruling us out of any team award.
Ken Miller, John Thresher, Mal Robinson and Bill Kerr are no respecters of reputation and will fight tooth and nail for Belgrave in any race going.
Ken Miller led the field after a quarter mile, but faded to finish 37th. Ventor (98th) ran below form and Joe Dooley, although making considerable ground in the latter stages, could only reach 106th.

Walker, vociferous before the start, revised his views after sampling the fast start and finished 100th, just ahead of Ken Miller (116), whilst Eric Gebbett (136) finished two places ahead of our recent county "vest" (!) Mal Robinson.
Ken Miller was a good third, with Thresher 7th, Walker 8th and Shippen 10th. The home teams were close winners from ourselves with S.L.H. third.
Our 4th place was by no means a disgrace, however, for despite being without the services of Newell and Miller our time was only a minute slower than last year's and was our third best ever.

After Bill's great effort had taken us to second, Clive Shippen was forced to give away two places and a very unfit Ken Miller another. Don Maclean took on the last leg run and easily held our fifth place.

Walker, John Thresher and Ron Linstead supported well but we had to wait some 20 places before Charlie Dabbs and Ken Miller appeared. Unfortunately Ken suffered a recurrence of his troublesome back injury.
Ken Miller has been completely out of training with severe back trouble, Alan Black with a fractured foot, and Charlie Dabbs is still travelling the long road back to fitness.

…ace with Bill Kerr 20th Ron Linstead 21st John Davies 24th and Clive Shippen not far away 30th. Our 6th scoring man was Ken Miller in 48th position. Ken was suffering agonies with a back injury but managed to keep going very pluckily.…

…the leading places with considerable vigour and success. 1962 however, was not to be our year for Bill Kerr, Alan Black,Ken Miller and Charlie Dabbs were all on the injured list and we had to call upon reserves who, although putting everything they had into their running, were not quite fit enough,…

In the absence of Barry Sawyer, Ken Miller, Clive Shippen, Laurie O'Hara, Derek Crookes and George Williams from the A team our hopes of a place as in the 1961 race were reduced to nil and the best we could do was to take 12th position out of the 69 teams that finished.
Then came a gap before Ken Miller appeared--Ken is slowly working his way back afer a long lay off through injury and by the time the big races come round should be a great force again.
Treasurer's report was made on Dave Shepherd's behalf by Ken Miller, one of the auditors. His lucid explanation of the balance sheet must surely brand him as the A.J.P.

Our congratulations are extended to Mike Smithers and Ken Miller on their recent marriages. Belgrave have been invited to compete in the 'Sward Trophy' meeting at the Polytechnic Stadium on July, 25th.

Dave Shepherd and Ken Miller presented the accounts for the year which showed the club was spending more than the income it was receiving. This could obviously not be allowed to continue and the members were warned that an increase in subscription was certainly on the cards next year.

Some 'old' hands turned out for this years race and it was a trip down memory lane as Pat O'Connor, Tony Fairclough, Ken Miller, Alan Black, Simon Holmes and George Flanagan crossed the finishing line.
Treasurer and explained many of the facets of the balance sheet which received and accepted with a vote of thanks to him and the two Auditors Ken Miller and Ron Conway.

Auditors, Ken Miller, has had a spell in hospital recently but we are pleased to be able to record that he is now on the mend again. There has been considerable speculation on the future of our Belgrave 20 mile road race.
Our two Honorary Auditors Ray Conway and Ken Miller have served the Club loyally for many years and feel that it is time to ease someone else into their shoes.
Auditors Ray Conway and Ken Miller, who between them seem to have put in so many years that it can't be true, were elected Life Members of Belgrave Harriers.

Ken Miller also went into hospital for an operation last September. Luckily he was not out of action for long because he was seen cheering on the Belgrave runners from his garden while they were contesting the Hog's Back Road Race.
